# Intake: Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U
**Issue Type:** bug
**Priority:** medium
**Discovered from:** WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish`'s live-repo mutation guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, consumed by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) fails a full-suite run whenever any non-worktree ref moves during the ~17-minute run. On a multi-agent host, concurrent agent activity moves `refs/heads/dev` (another agent's finish fast-forward on the shared main checkout), `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and other `refs/remotes/origin/*` (concurrent fetch/push), and siblings' feature-branch refs — none of which the current exclusion covers. The result is a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict while the canonical suite itself passes, forcing a wasted ~17-minute run: the item resets to `open`, the agent must re-sync and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `implement.py finish` or `/skill:test` on a shared multi-agent host; the guard's false positive blocks their release gate.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the finish-gate verdict as the pre-push signal for `dev`.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of `git_sandbox.py` and the two guards (F4 outer `run_tests.py`, F5 inner conftest/`live_repo_guard.py`) that share the helper.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the finish-gate full-suite run to stay green while sibling agents advance `dev`, fetch/push to `origin`, or move their own branch refs, so that concurrent activity on the shared host does not nullify a ~17-minute run.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class), so real corruption is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want the exclusion contract documented and regression-tested at both helper and guard level, so the two consumers cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A snapshot diff in which **only** `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, or `refs/remotes/origin/*` moved (working tree and non-excluded config unchanged) reports `changed == false`; `fingerprint()` agrees. Regression tests cover each ref class (local `dev`, remote-tracking `dev`, arbitrary `origin/*`).
- [ ] AC2 — Genuine mutations are **still** detected and fail the guard: a new/removed/moved ref outside the excluded set (e.g. fixture branch creation like the 2026-09-24 incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), a non-excluded local-config rewrite, and any working-tree change. No behaviour of the existing agent-worktree / `refs/worklog/*` exclusions regresses.
- [ ] AC3 — `guarded_run_all` (the `implement.py finish` test gate) and the inner per-test guard both pass in a deterministic regression test that moves `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/dev` mid-run on a `tmp_path` sandbox, while the same harness still fails when a genuine mutation (e.g. a new non-excluded branch) is introduced.
- [ ] AC4 — The exclusion contract is documented in the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8, naming exactly which ref namespaces are excluded and why concurrent collaborative movement cannot be distinguished from suite-caused moves of those refs (residual-risk note).
- [ ] AC5 — Full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the new changes; new regression tests live with the existing guard tests (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` as appropriate).

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` remains **stdlib-only**, loadable by file location (repo-root `conftest.py` uses `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`; no `sys.path` mutation).
- Exclusions stay **derived from git plumbing**, never a `wl-*` name pattern (documented reason: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches).
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands, never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch` or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not silently disable detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX leak class (see AC2). Excluding a ref namespace is only acceptable where concurrent-agent movement and suite-caused movement are genuinely indistinguishable *and* the incident signature remains detectable through the other surfaces (working tree, config, non-excluded refs).
- Any extra git invocation must stay cheap and confined to the snapshot path; the per-test fingerprint must not become a full `status` scan.
- Implementation happens in the **SorraAgents** repo (the global-skills home where `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` lives), tracked via the ContextHub worklog — precedent: WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 committed to SorraAgents.

## Existing state

- `snapshot_repo_state` captures refs (via `for-each-ref`, dropping `refs/worklog/*`), local config, registered worktrees and working-tree status; `diff_snapshots` filters out `excluded_refs` = branches checked out in worktrees under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` (union of both snapshots' sets) plus the `branch.<name>.remote`/`branch.<name>.merge` config those worktrees own.
- `main_checkout_root()` already anchors the exclusion on the main checkout so `implement.py finish` (which runs the suite from a linked worktree) excludes sibling worktrees — delivered by SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 / SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65.
- **Gap:** refs the shared host moves concurrently are not under `.worklog/worktrees/`, so they are not excluded: `refs/heads/dev` (main checkout's checked-out branch; another agent's finish fast-forwards it), `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, all other `refs/remotes/origin/*`, and any sibling feature branch not currently registered in a `.worklog/worktrees/` worktree.
- Observed on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6: `refs/remotes/origin/dev` bbc8e89a → 4163175, `refs/heads/dev` advanced, and a sibling's feature-branch ref moved; both declared suite commands exited 0 yet the gate failed.

## Desired change

- Extend the exclusion contract so refs that concurrent agent activity legitimately moves cannot fail the gate: at minimum `refs/remotes/origin/*` (remote-tracking refs — only `fetch`/`pull`/`push` move them, never a hermetic fixture) and the integration branch `refs/heads/dev` (advanced by siblings' finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout). Sibling feature-branch refs are already excluded while registered as agent worktrees; handle any residual unchecked-out sibling branch movement if the implementer can do so without a `wl-*` name pattern.
- Tighter alternative (if preferred by the implementer): scope the ref-check to the refs a suite could plausibly touch (e.g. ignore ref *moves* but still report ref *additions*), while keeping config + working-tree detection intact.
- Add regression tests at the helper level (`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`) and across both guards (`guarded_run_all` and the per-test conftest guard), using the existing hermetic `git_sandbox` factories under `tmp_path` — never the live checkout.
- Update `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 and the `git_sandbox.py` docstring to state the extended exclusion contract and the residual risk.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Extend the exclusion set (e.g. `refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/dev`) in `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`; document the contract in the module docstring.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Helper-level regression tests for dev/remote-tracking ref movement (no diff) and non-excluded ref moves (still reported).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Guard-level tests: mid-run `dev`/`origin/dev` movement does not trip the inner guard; a genuine non-excluded ref adds/moves still fails.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` / `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — Verify `guarded_run_all` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused regression test if needed.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — §8 exclusion contract update (refs excluded for concurrency reasons + residual risk).
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — Only if the outer/inner guard needs a code change beyond the shared helper (prefer helper-only so consumers cannot drift).

## Related work

- `WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6` — source session where the false positive was observed twice (discovered-from).
- `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627` — predecessor false positive: linked-worktree anchoring; fixed by the `main_checkout_root()` helper this item builds on.
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — 2026-09-26 `GIT_DIR` leak incident; the guard's reason to exist; the mutation-detection this item must not weaken.
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — origin of `git_sandbox.py` (remote `dev` corruption / test isolation); snapshot design source.
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` / `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — outer (`run_tests.py`) and inner (conftest) live-repo guards.
- `SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65` — superseding producer decision for the worktree-registration churn false positive (same guard path).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and the snapshot/exclusion contract this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** excluding `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `refs/heads/dev` from the diff is acceptable because those refs' concurrent movement is indistinguishable from suite-caused movement, and exhaustive ref-based detection is replaced by config/working-tree/non-excluded-ref detection for those namespaces. If the producer prefers full-strength ref detection, the alternative is the tighter scoping (AC2 language) or running the suite under a repo lock.
- **Risk (false negative):** an overly broad exclusion hides a genuine incident signature. Mitigation: the incident class always also rewrites config and/or working tree (still detected); AC2 pins the incident signature detection.
- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into refactoring the guard or adding a repo lock. Recorded as out of scope; a lock or serialisation idea can be linked as a follow-up work item.
- **Risk (performance):** the per-test fingerprint must stay cheap; any exclusion-list computation must not add a full `status` scan per test.
- **Risk (drift):** two consumers share the helper; keep the change helper-only so `run_tests.py` and the conftest guard cannot drift (AC3).
- **Residual risk:** two agents running `finish` concurrently can still contend on the same worktree/branch; excluded at the shared-ref level here, not solved (separate concern).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6) already contained the problem, observed evidence, impact, possible fix directions and a workaround. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Which repo owns the fix?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` and the guards live in the **SorraAgents** repo (global skills home; ContextHub's `skill/shared` is an untracked symlink to it). The work item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog; precedent WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 was implemented and committed in SorraAgents with the item tracked from ContextHub. Evidence: `git ls-files skill/` in ContextHub (8 files, none under `skill/shared`), `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills` = SorraAgents, commit `6229a060` message.
- Q: "Can the fix simply ignore ref movement entirely?" — Answer (agent, analysis): the safer middle ground is excluding only concurrency-moved namespaces (`refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/dev`) while keeping detection of new/removed non-excluded refs (fixture branches), config and working-tree changes — the incident signature never moves *only* `dev` without also changing config/tree. Recorded as an assumption (see Risks); preferred fix direction per the source item's "Possible fix".
- Q: "Does the inner per-test guard need its own change?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): prefer a helper-only change; `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` (F5) and `run_tests.py` (F4) both consume `fingerprint`/`diff_snapshots`, so a helper-level fix propagates to both without drift (SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65, §8.1 contract).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS9PL90F002MR8G** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs in global ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md (completed)
- **WL-0MSUEO1U60072GNK** – Tests: identity gate unit + CLI suite (TDD red) (completed)
- **WL-0MRIEPH3J006RAPL** – wl sync corrupts dev branch when run from git worktree (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: active, advanced, agent, another, branch (+87 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: active, agent, another, branch, cache (+86 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: active, activity, agent, another, branch (+79 more)

> Automated matches are low-confidence (generic terms). The hand-curated related work above is authoritative.

# Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, I want an explicit per-item way to pause automatic scheduling — by assigning the item to myself — that does not rely on a magic DB flag, with a well-known sentinel value the release gate can recognise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Assign item to producer ⇒ no tier auto-dispatches it (claims fail stale at every tier) — the scheduling hold works.
  _(Parent epic AC restated verbatim; this child is the covering work item.)_

- [ ] Epic open question Q2 is answered and recorded: the literal producer-hold value is a reserved, well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity (self-describing, reusable by the release gate). **Recommended:** reserved identity value, exact literal confirmed with the producer.
- [ ] The convention is documented: a non-empty assignee means "intentionally held from auto-dispatch"; assigning to the producer is the per-item pause switch.
- [ ] Every ContextHub/SorraAgents assignee writer is audited (intake, plan, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`, `status_lifecycle`) and clears the assignee on session end; `status_lifecycle`'s failure-exit already clears it.
- [ ] A test proves that clearing a claim's assignee makes the item dispatchable again (hold released).
- [ ] Correctness risk R1 is addressed by the clearing-discipline audit (no writer silently suppresses auto-dispatch).

## Constraints

- The sentinel must not collide with real agent identities.
- Must not strand in-flight implement/plan/intake claims: only session-end clearing is added.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents)
- `./AGENTS.md` (draft claim/hold pattern; finalised in C12)

## Deliverables

Sentinel decision, convention documentation, clearing-discipline changes, test.

# Feature: Exclude dev + remote-tracking refs from guard diff

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** feature (implementation slice)

## Summary

Helper-only change in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`: `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` ignore the `refs/heads/dev` ref and the whole `refs/remotes/origin/*` namespace, so concurrent movement of these refs by sibling agents (finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout, concurrent fetch/push) can no longer fail the live-repo mutation guard. Because both consumers (F4 outer `run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`, F5 inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`) share the helper, neither needs a code change and they cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` both report no change when only `refs/heads/dev` and/or `refs/remotes/origin/*` refs moved (movement or churn inside those namespaces is invisible).
- [ ] AC2 — Every other ref addition/removal/movement (e.g. fixture-branch creation like the incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), every local-config rewrite outside excluded branches, and every working-tree change still reports `changed == true` and fails the guard.
- [ ] AC3 — Existing exclusions are behaviour-preserving: `refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree branch refs plus their `branch.<name>.*` config, and main-checkout anchoring all behave as before (existing regression tests stay green).
- [ ] AC4 — Helper-only: no consumer code change in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` or `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`; the F1 guard-level regression tests (inner + outer) pass via the shared helper.
- [ ] AC5 — Exclusion is expressed as ref-namespace constants (`refs/remotes/origin/` prefix, `refs/heads/dev` exact) — never a `wl-*` name pattern; snapshots stay read-only plumbing; the per-test `fingerprint` stays cheap (no `status` scan).
- [ ] AC6 — The full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the change.

## Target outcome

`implement.py finish` and `/skill:test` stay green on a shared multi-agent host while siblings move `dev`/`origin/*`; genuine in-place checkout mutation (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class) still fails the gate.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- F1 helper + guard tests pass.
- Adversary tests still fail on genuine mutations.
- Full suite green.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add module constants (e.g. `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_NAMESPACES = ("refs/remotes/origin/",)` and `CONCURRENCY_EXCLUDED_REF_EXACT = "refs/heads/dev"`) plus one shared predicate `_is_concurrency_excluded_ref(ref)`.
- Apply the predicate to the ref filter in `diff_snapshots` (alongside the existing `excluded` set) and to the ref tuple in `fingerprint`. Keep raw refs in the snapshot for diagnostics/`describe_diff`.
- Verify no `branch.dev.*` config exclusion is required (dev-tracking config is static and not churned by a ref fast-forward); add it only if a guard test demonstrates churn.
- Run F1: helper + guard tests flip red → green.

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` stays stdlib-only and loadable by file location (no `sys.path` mutation).
- Exclusion derived from git plumbing/ref-namespace constants, never a `wl-*` name pattern.
- The fix must not silently disable detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX leak class (AC2; config + working-tree + non-excluded ref surfaces still fire).

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`

## Dependencies

- The F1 regression-tests item — this implementation turns F1's red tests green (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- `git_sandbox.py` exclusion change; F1 regression tests green.

# Feature: Document excluded refs contract and residual risk

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** docs

## Summary

Update `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 and the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring so the exclusion contract names exactly which ref namespaces are excluded (now including `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*`), why concurrent-agent movement of those refs is indistinguishable from suite-caused movement, and what residual risk remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 lists every excluded ref namespace (`refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree refs, `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/*`) with the rationale that concurrent collaborative movement of those refs cannot be distinguished from suite-caused movement (residual-risk note).
- [ ] AC2 — The `git_sandbox.py` module docstring states the same extended exclusion contract so the helper is self-documenting for both consumers.
- [ ] AC3 — Residual risks are documented: (i) a sibling agent's unregistered feature-branch move can still trip the gate; (ii) a `refs/heads/dev`-only movement is no longer a standalone incident signal — the leak class is still caught via config + working-tree + non-excluded ref surfaces (cross-reference §8.4 / §9 and SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX).

## Target outcome

Maintainers can reason about the guard's blind spots; the two consumers cannot drift because the contract lives next to the single shared helper.

## Definition of done (pass/fail)

- §8 and docstring updated and cross-referenced; no code behaviour change.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the §8.1 surfaces list and add a residual-risk paragraph in §8 naming the two exclusions added for concurrency reasons.
- Update the module docstring's residual-risk paragraph to name the new exclusions and cross-reference §8.4/§9.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (docstring only)

## Dependencies

- The F2 implementation item — documents its exclusion contract.

## Deliverables

- Updated §8 and module docstring.

# F1: Classification and replacement audit (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (verification-first — the analysis gate for the migration)

## Goal

Produce the authoritative classification table (parent AC1) covering **all 137**
`toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences across the 14 `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`
files, post it as a work-item comment, and prove that every `migrate` occurrence has a
named observable-outcome replacement (parent AC4's replacement-traceability requirement).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A classification table is posted as a comment on WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM with one row per
   occurrence: file, line, category (`retain` / `migrate`), and a one-line reason.
2. The 137 rows reconcile exactly to the documented per-file baseline
   (dispatch 37, audit-tier 22, critical-first 21, tiers 15, pane 14, downtime-worker.test 13,
   sprint-view 8, orchestrator 3, settings 2, parse 2), including the 18 `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`
   and 8 `.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` forms.
3. Classification follows the producer-approved rule (WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM, plan Q1 answer **A**):
   - `retain` — calls on injected `deps`/boundary adapters (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`,
     `closePane`, `spawnFn`, `dep`, anchor/reaper lookups, …), observable output streams
     (`stderrSpy`), and injected `fetcher` / `onProxyIdle` `callback` (sole observable channel
     for the asserted effect), plus `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` ordering assertions unless an
     outcome assertion proves identical ordering (producer Q1-A scope decision).
   - `migrate` — `handle.once('error'|'exit', …)` shape wiring where the same test drives the
     listener and asserts the resulting `spawned` outcome, plus redundant query-call assertions
     whose behaviour is already proven by a returned outcome/state.
4. Every `migrate` row names the observable-outcome assertion (existing, or to be added in F2)
   that replaces it.
5. No occurrence is silently dropped: category counts sum to the baseline total per file.

## Constraints

- Analysis and table only — **no test-file edits in this step**.
- UK English throughout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — 37 occurrences (largest)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — 22 occurrences, stderrSpy rows
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` — 21 occurrences
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — 14 occurrences, 4 `handle.once` wiring rows
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — 15 occurrences (Nth ordering rows)

## Deliverables

- Work-item comment with the reconciliation-checked classification table
- Data (comment id) for F3 to consume and F4 to verify against

# F2: Strengthen observable-outcome assertions (test-first)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (test-first — assertions land before any removal)

## Goal

For every occurrence classified `migrate` in F1 whose behaviour is **not** already proven by an
existing observable-outcome assertion, add the outcome assertion **first** (TDD ordering), so F3
can remove the internal/redundant call-shape assertion without weakening regression coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each `migrate` occurrence that F1 identified as lacking equivalent outcome coverage now has a
   new assertion on a returned value/state (e.g. `spawned`, `outcome`, poll result) that proves
   the same behaviour.
2. All new assertions assert observable results — none of them assert mock call shape via
   `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.
3. The test-case count in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` is unchanged.
4. Only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files (and inline comments) change; no
   production-code change.
5. The target file's test suite passes (via the test skill) after the additions.

## Notes

- If F1 finds that **every** `migrate` occurrence already has equivalent outcome coverage (the
  4 `handle.once` wiring cases drive their listeners and assert `spawned`; redundant query rows
  assert `outcome.kind`/`outcome.candidate`), the deliverable is a short comment recording that
  no new assertions are required, and F3 proceeds with removal only. This satisfies the
  test-first requirement because the replacement assertions already exist in the same tests.

## Constraints

- Test-first: additions precede any removals in F3.
- UK English throughout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — 4 `handle.once` wiring cases (lines ~100–150)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — redundant `getNextItem` query rows

## Deliverables

- New/changed observable-outcome assertions (or the no-op conclusion comment)

# F3: Migrate internal/redundant assertions; annotate retained (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (implementation — the migration itself)

## Goal

Convert every occurrence classified `migrate` in F1 so the same behaviour is asserted through an
observable outcome, or removed where an existing assertion in the same test already proves that
behaviour (F2/table). Add a short inline justification comment to every retained assertion
(parent AC3), so the remaining 100+ dependency-call assertions are auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `migrate` occurrence is converted/removed per the F1 table; the table names the outcome
   assertion that replaces each removed assertion.
2. Verification: `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith' packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`
   returns **zero** matches.
3. Every retained occurrence carries an inline comment stating why the dependency call is the
   unit's observable contract (producer Q2-A: inline comment per retained assertion).
4. No test case is deleted — the test-case count is unchanged; only assertions move/change form.
5. Only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files change (plus inline comments); no
   production-code change; no new test dependencies.
6. The affected test files pass (via the test skill) with the changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve test semantics: no assertion is dropped without a named replacement or an explicit
  table justification.
- Retained ordering assertions (`toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` proving tier/fallback order) stay
  unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering.
- UK English throughout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — migrate 4 `handle.once` wiring assertions
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — migrate redundant query-call assertions
- all 14 `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files — annotate retained assertions inline

## Deliverables

- Edited test files with migrated assertions and inline justifications
- Zero `handle.once`-`toHaveBeenCalledWith` matches (rg verification)

# F4: Verify migration and close parent AC4 (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (verification + parent evidence)

## Goal

Verify the migration end-to-end (parent AC4/AC6) and post the evidence comment on the split
parent WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX closing deferred AC4 (parent AC5, producer Q3-A) — without reopening
or re-auditing that parent.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Behavioural coverage preserved (AC4):** the test-case count per
   `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` file is identical to the `b195e01a` baseline; a thin diff against
   the baseline commit shows only assertion/comment changes, no `it(`/`test(` lines deleted.
2. **Scope confined:** `git diff` touches only `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`
   files (no production-code change) — verified by `--stat` against
   `b195e01a` (or HEAD).
3. **Zero internal-wiring assertions (AC2):** `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith'`
   returns zero matches.
4. **Documentation and full suite (AC6):** related documentation and code comments updated to
   reflect the migration; the full project test suite passes via `/skill:test`.
5. **Parent AC4 evidence (AC5, Q3-A):** an evidence comment is posted on WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX
   linking WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM and its outcome; the parent is NOT reopened or re-audited.
6. **Classification table closed:** the F1 comment's per-file category counts reconcile to the
   post-migration file state.

## Constraints

- Do not modify production code or non-downtime-worker test files.
- The parent (WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX) stays `completed`/`done`.
- UK English throughout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (14 files, verification targets)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` (read-only reference)
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (reference; no change expected)

## Deliverables

- Verification report comment (counts, diff scope, rg checks, suite result)
- Evidence comment on WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX (parent AC4 closed)

## Appendix: Plan clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-15)

- Q: "The incident included an unregistered sibling feature-branch ref move. Given AC1/AC2 forbid excluding all of `refs/heads/*` and forbid a `wl-*` name pattern, what should the exclusion breadth be?" Options: (a) exact namespace exclusion — ignore only `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*`; (b) move-insensitivity — ignore ref *moves* in any namespace, still report additions/removals. **Recommended:** (a). — Answer (producer): deferred to the recommendation. **Final: (a)**. Rationale: (a) is AC-literal, keeps moved-ref detection maximal outside the two named namespaces; (b) would require amending AC2 and weaken the moved-ref surface. Research: repo inspection of `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`), `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8, and the three guard test files. Source: interactive reply.

- Q (resolved by repo investigation, no producer input needed): "Does the inner per-test guard or the outer guard need its own code change?" — Answer (agent): No. Both consume the shared `git_sandbox.py` helper, so a helper-only change propagates without drift (AC4, SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65 §8.1). Source: `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.

- Q (resolved by repo investigation): "Is a `branch.dev.*` config exclusion also required?" — Answer (agent): Not expected — `branch.dev.remote`/`branch.dev.merge` are static and are not churned by a ref fast-forward; the F2 item verifies and only adds the exclusion if a guard test demonstrates churn. Source: `_excluded_branch_config_prefixes` in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`.

No OPEN QUESTIONs remain.

**Q2 answered — producer-hold sentinel:** reserved sentinel $PRODUCER_HOLD_ASSIGNEE = 'Map' (the producer's wl identity), exported from packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts with isProducerHold(). It never collides with automated agent identities (pi/implement/@github-copilot); comparison is exact and whitespace-tolerant.

**Scheduling-hold convention (AC1/AC3):** a non-empty assignee holds the item from auto-dispatch at every tier — select* helpers filter isAssigneeHeld, classifyItemForDispatch returns null, and the audit claim's --if-assignee "" CAS fails stale. Assigning to the producer is the per-item pause switch; clearing the assignee releases it (AC5 tested).

**Assignee-writer clearing-discipline audit (AC4/R1):** status_lifecycle failure-exit already clears assignee (SorraAgents). herdr claim/rollback clears on every terminal dispatch outcome (covering child WL-0MV85WD400091OZ6). Residual non-empty-assignee writers to keep tracking: delegate @github-copilot (github.js) and interview.ts — both noted for the C12 docs wrap; the ship-gate re-home is SA-tracked (C8).
